mcqs.question: A 60‑W bulb and a 100‑W bulb are both connected to the same 120‑V supply. Which statement correctly compares their power ratings?

options.A: The 60‑W bulb consumes more electrical energy per second than the 100‑W bulb.
options.B: The 100‑W bulb converts more electrical energy into light and heat per second than the 60‑W bulb.
options.C: Both bulbs have the same power rating because they are connected to the same voltage.
options.D: Power rating depends on the colour of the bulb, not its wattage.

mcqs.answer: The 100‑W bulb converts more electrical energy into light and heat per second than the 60‑W bulb.
mcqs.explanation: Power rating (in watts) tells how much energy a device uses or converts each second. A 100‑W bulb uses 100 joules per second, which is greater than the 60 joules per second used by a 60‑W bulb. Hence option B is correct; the other options misinterpret the meaning of power rating.

mcqs.question: If a machine does 200 joules of work in 4 seconds, which of the following best defines the power of the machine?

options.A: Power is the total work done by the machine.
options.B: Power is the rate at which work is done.
options.C: Power is the amount of energy stored in the machine.
options.D: Power is the force applied by the machine.

mcqs.answer: Power is the rate at which work is done.
mcqs.explanation: Power is defined as the amount of work done (or energy transferred) per unit time, mathematically P = Work/Time. In the scenario, the machine’s power is 200 J / 4 s = 50 W, illustrating the definition in option B. Options A, C, and D describe different concepts.

mcqs.question: A person lifts a 20‑kg box to a height of 2 m in 5 seconds. What is the power output? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Work done = m g h = 20 kg × 10 m/s² × 2 m = 400 J. Power = Work/Time = 400 J ÷ 5 s = 80 W. The common misconception is to think that lifting faster automatically doubles power without considering the work done; the correct calculation gives 80 W.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand watt as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the unit "watt" is correct?

options.B: 1 watt equals 1 newton metre per second.
options.C: 1 watt equals 1 kilogram metre squared per second cubed.

mcqs.explanation: The watt (W) is the SI unit of power. By definition, 1 W = 1 J/s. Since 1 J = 1 N·m, it is also 1 N·m/s. In base SI units, 1 W = 1 kg·m²/s³. Therefore all three expressions are equivalent, making option D correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to work and time
mcqs.question: Machine A does 500 J of work in 10 s, while Machine B does 300 J of work in 5 s. Which statement is true?

options.A: Machine A has higher power than Machine B.
options.B: Machine B has higher power than Machine A.
options.C: Both machines have the same power.
options.D: Power cannot be compared without knowing the forces involved.

mcqs.answer: Machine B has higher power than Machine A.
mcqs.explanation: Power = Work/Time. Machine A: 500 J / 10 s = 50 W. Machine B: 300 J / 5 s = 60 W. Since 60 W > 50 W, Machine B has the higher power. Option B is correct; the other options misinterpret the relationship.

mcqs.question: A 1500‑W heater and a 750‑W fan are operated on a 230‑V supply. Which device draws a larger current?

options.A: The heater draws a larger current.
options.B: The fan draws a larger current.
options.C: Both draw the same current because they are on the same voltage.
options.D: Current cannot be determined without knowing the resistance of each device.

mcqs.answer: The heater draws a larger current.
mcqs.explanation: Current I = Power / Voltage. Heater: I = 1500 W / 230 V ≈ 6.52 A. Fan: I = 750 W / 230 V ≈ 3.26 A. The heater therefore draws about twice the current of the fan. Option A is correct; the other options ignore the power‑current relationship.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines power?

options.A: Power is the ability to do work.
options.B: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy.
options.C: Power is the same as energy.

mcqs.answer: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy.
mcqs.explanation: Power quantifies how quickly work is done or energy is transferred, expressed as P = Work/Time (or Energy/Time). Option B captures this definition. Option A describes capability, not rate; option C confuses power with energy; option D misstates the unit (joules measure energy, not power).

mcqs.question: A motor lifts a 5‑kg load through a height of 3 m in 2 seconds. What is the power output? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Work done = m g h = 5 kg × 10 m/s² × 3 m = 150 J. Power = Work/Time = 150 J ÷ 2 s = 75 W. Hence option A is correct; the other options result from incorrect division or omission of the height factor.
